title: A figure from a dream
subtitle: Meet someone or something from a dream — not to decode it, to hear it.

steps.body:
We're not here to decode your dream, or decide what the symbols 'mean.'

We're here to meet a figure from it — as if it were real and had something to say. Dreams speak in their own language; meeting one is enough.

If you're feeling far from yourself right now, this can wait. The Support tab is there.
Ready to begin? You can stop here anytime.

steps.title: Bring to mind a figure or image from a recent dream — one that stayed with you.
steps.body: A person, a creature, a place, an object. Give it a name to call it by.
steps.placeholder: The stranger, the locked door, the animal…

steps.title: Describe it as you saw it.
steps.body: Don't interpret — just describe. What it looked like, how it moved, the feeling around it.

steps.title: Does it feel old or young — ancient, or new?
When you bring it to mind now, where do you feel it in your body?
steps.placeholder: Chest, gut, throat, nowhere in particular…

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let the figure speak. Don't decide in advance what it says. What does it want you to know?
steps.hint: Resist the urge to interpret. Just let it talk.

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Ask it: why did you come to me? Write its answer.

steps.body: Stay with what it said. No need to make sense of it yet.

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let it tell you one more thing before it goes.

steps.title: What does this figure seem to want from you — or want you to see?
steps.body: Not a translation. Just what you sense it's asking.

exit.body: Dreams speak in their own language. You don't have to translate it — meeting it is enough. It may keep speaking, in time.
